- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.20) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.15), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% if price is falling sharply.  
- Model frequently overshoots after recent spikes (e.g., +5%+ above 70) — cap forecast at +3% above peak unless sentiment is strong bullish.  
- If 3+ consecutive forecast days show downward trend, model often fails to reverse — add 0.5–1.5% upward bias if sentiment turns positive.  
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above 30-day average, reduce by 1–2% unless sentiment supports continuation.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often lags 1–2 days in reaction to sentiment shifts — adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead if sentiment changes sharply.
